papers.title: Honeysuckle extract attenuates lung ischemia-reperfusion injury: Involvement of TLR4/NF-κB signaling.
papers.authors: Zhao Y, Ren K, Liu B, Wang L, Qiao Y, Xiao X et al.
papers.abstract:
Lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI) is the leading cause of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplantation, with very limited targeted therapeutic options. Honeysuckle (Lonicera japonica Thunb.; Caprifoliaceae) is a classic traditional Chinese herbal medicine with heat-clearing and detoxifying effects, which has been widely applied to treat various pulmonary inflammatory diseases. However, its potential role in LIRI remains unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of honeysuckle extract against LIRI and explore the potential mechanisms underlying these effects.
The chemical constituents of honeysuckle extract were analyzed by ultra-high performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Network pharmacology was utilized to predict its potential therapeutic targets and related signaling pathways. A BEAS-2B hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) injury model and a rat LIRI model were established to evaluate the effects of honeysuckle extract pretreatment, and the levels of oxidative stress-related biomarkers and inflammatory cytokines were detected. Subsequently, techniques including quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), Western blotting, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence were applied to verify its pulmonary protective mechanism, and transcriptomics and molecular docking were performed to provide exploratory evidence.
A total of 91 constituents were preliminarily identified by UHPLC-MS/MS, mainly flavonoids, terpenoids and polyphenols. Network pharmacology predicted that TLR4/NF-κB was one of the core signaling pathways involved in LIRI. In H/R-stimulated BEAS-2B cells, honeysuckle extract improved cell viability, reduced intracellular oxidant-sensitive fluorescence and attenuated oxidative stress, restored antioxidant capacity, inhibited the production of pro-inflammatory mediators, and suppressed the activation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB cascade. In LIRI model rats, honeysuckle pretreatment alleviated pulmonary edema and histopathological damage, restored pulmonary redox homeostasis, and decreased the levels of IL-6, IL-1β and TNF-α. Meanwhile, it downregulated the expression of TLR4 in lung tissues and reduced NF-κB p65-associated fluorescence intensity in lung tissues. Transcriptomic analysis identified 346 differentially expressed genes, which were significantly enriched in the Toll-like receptor, NF-κB signaling pathway and TNF signaling pathway. Molecular docking generated predicted poses and scores for morroniside and chlorogenic acid against TLR4-, MyD88-, and NF-κB p65-associated receptor models. These calculations do not demonstrate direct binding or establish which compounds account for the effects of the whole extract.
In the experimental models used, honeysuckle extract pretreatment was associated with reduced indices of oxidative stress, inflammation, and lung tissue injury. Attenuated TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling accompanied these effects, but pathway dependence was not established. These findings support further evaluation of honeysuckle extract as a potential preconditioning intervention for LIRI.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Ameliorates Ulcerative Colitis Through Multi-target Regulation of the NLRP3 Inflammasome: A Systematic Review.
papers.authors: Li X, Ma D, Wang Y, Bai M, Zhou Y, Li Y et al.
papers.abstract:
In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), ulcerative colitis (UC)-like manifestations are commonly related to diarrhea, dysentery, chronic dysentery, and hematochezia. Classical prescriptions and medicinal materials used for these conditions are increasingly investigated for their capacity to regulate the NLRP3 inflammasome, a central inflammatory platform in UC.
This review aims to elucidate the regulatory mechanisms of the NLRP3 inflammasome in the pathophysiology of UC and to systematically analyze the pharmacological mechanisms underlying TCM-mediated modulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome for UC amelioration.
Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, and MEDLINE were searched using the combined keywords "NLRP3 inflammasome," "traditional Chinese medicine," and "ulcerative colitis" and relevant intervention names. A systematic review was conducted on animal and cell studies that met the criteria.
The available evidence indicates that TCM interventions can attenuate NLRP3 activation and downstream Caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, enhance autophagy and mitophagy, regulate gut microbiota-derived metabolites, reduce mitochondrial oxidative stress, and influence upstream pathways including NF-κB, TLR4/MyD88, TXNIP, AMPK/ULK1, PINK1/Parkin, AhR, and Nrf2. However, most evidence is preclinical; clinical confirmation, standardized preparations, exposure-response data, and rigorous safety assessment remain limited.
TCM provides an ethnopharmacologically grounded source of multi-component interventions targeting the NLRP3-centered inflammatory network in UC. Future studies should directly connect traditional indications with authenticated botanical sources, standardized chemical profiles, clinically relevant dosing, and well-designed randomized trials.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture Alleviates Neuropathic Pain in Rats by Regulating the Camk4-Ehmt2/G9a-Oprm1 Axis.
papers.authors: Huang H, Liu L, Lan Y, Shang H, Yang S, Li G
papers.abstract:
Neuropathic pain (NP) is a common type of chronic pain in clinical practice, for which current therapeutic options remain limited. Electroacupuncture (EA) shows promising therapeutic potential, but its underlying molecular mechanisms are yet to be fully elucidated.
A rat model of NP was established by chronic constriction injury (CCI) of the sciatic nerve, and pain behaviors were assessed by measuring paw withdrawal thresholds to mechanical stimuli. EA was applied to the ipsilateral acupoints Zusanli (ST36) and Yanglingquan (GB34). Pharmacological inhibitors, high-throughput RNA sequencing, Western blotting, and qRT-PCR were comprehensively employed to explore the molecular mechanisms underlying EA-induced relief of NP.
EA significantly attenuated mechanical hypersensitivity in CCI rats. On day 14, EA significantly increased the 50% PWT compared with both BC (P < 0.0001) and SA (P < 0.05) (no significant change was observed in the sham group). Mechanistically, the previously reported DS-LncRNA in mice was not detected in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) of CCI rats. Instead, EA significantly upregulated Camk4 and Oprm1 and downregulated Ehmt2/G9a at both mRNA and protein levels compared with BC (P < 0.001) and SA (P < 0.05)(except sham group), and these changes were associated with alleviation of NP progression.
EA alleviates NP in CCI rats by regulating the Camk4-Ehmt2/G9a-Oprm1 axis, including upregulation of Camk4 and suppression of Ehmt2/G9a-mediated repression of Oprm1. Camk4 and Ehmt2/G9a may serve as potential novel therapeutic targets for NP management; however, the BRD4770-induced partial restoration of Camk4 suggests possible feedback regulation between Ehmt2/G9a and Camk4, whether Camk4 directly and causally regulates Ehmt2/G9a requires further rescue experiments.

papers.title: Integrated rehabilitation for post-stroke anxiety: a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial.
papers.authors: Xu S, Ye K, Zhang S, Chen K, Zhou J, Hu X et al.
papers.abstract:
Post-stroke anxiety (PSA) affects approximately one-quarter of stroke survivors and impedes functional recovery, yet pharmacological options remain limited by inconsistent efficacy and absent standardized guidelines. This study evaluated an integrated rehabilitation program combining repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), acupuncture, and Chinese herbal medicine for PSA.
In this multicenter randomized controlled trial, 188 participants with mild-to-moderate PSA were randomized 1:1 to standard care (pharmacotherapy, general care, and exercise therapy) or integrated rehabilitation (standard care plus rTMS, acupuncture, and Chinese herbal medicine) for 4 weeks, with an 8-week follow-up. The primary outcome was the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A). Secondary outcomes included the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Activities of Daily Living (ADL), Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Analyses followed an intention-to-treat framework.
The integrated rehabilitation group showed significantly greater reductions in HAM-A scores at Week 4 than controls (between-group difference, 2.49 points; 95% CI, 1.50 to 3.48; p <0.01), and this treatment benefit was maintained at week 12 (p<0.01). In supportive analyses of the secondary outcomes, Holm-adjusted group × time interactions remained significant for PSQI, MoCA, upper-extremity motor function, ADL, and SAS scores (all adjusted p<0.05), but not for lower-extremity motor function or IADL.
The integrated rehabilitation program improved the primary anxiety outcome and provided supportive evidence of broader clinical benefits in sleep quality, cognition, and upper-extremity motor function, together with distinct patterns of functional change in ADL and IADL. Overall, these findings support further consideration of this integrated approach as an adjunct to pharmacotherapy for PSA. Biological mechanisms and contributions of individual intervention components remain undetermined. Further mechanistic investigations incorporating biological measures would help clarify the underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: Effect of auricular acupressure on labour analgesia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Bai R, Tian M, Wang Y, Yang Y, Yang C
papers.abstract:
Labour pain significantly influences maternal childbirth experiences and outcomes. Auricular acupressure has shown potential as a non-pharmacological method for labour analgesia. However, comprehensive evidence regarding its efficacy across distinct stages of Labour-specifically the latent and active phases remain unclear, and optimal practice protocols require further clarification.
Computerized searches of Chinese and English databases were conducted to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining auricular acupressure for labour analgesia. Meta-analyses were performed using RevMan 5.4 software. Primary analyses were stratified by labour stage (latent vs. active phase), supplemented with subgroup analyses based on acupoint number, practitioner training, and the timing of outcome measurement.
Auricular acupressure significantly reduced pain during both the latent phase (SMD = -2.89, 95% CI: -4.03 to -1.75; P < 0.001) and the active phase (SMD = -1.62, 95% CI: -2.37 to -0.87; P < 0.001). During the latent phase, stimulation of six or more auricular points produced a greater analgesic effect (SMD = -4.13) than stimulation of fewer than six points (SMD = -2.38). During the active phase, fewer than six points showed a numerically greater effect (SMD = -1.83) than six or more points (SMD = -1.60), but this finding was unstable in sensitivity analyses. Studies reporting trained providers showed greater pain reduction (SMD = -1.97 vs. -1.30), although the between-subgroup difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.38), and only one latent-phase study reported formal practitioner training.
Auricular acupressure may reduce labour pain and may be useful as a non-pharmacological adjunct to routine care. However, the certainty of these findings is limited by predictable allocation in two studies, incomplete reporting of blinding, and substantial heterogeneity. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of effectiveness.

papers.title: Acupoint injection therapy: A web of science-based bibliometric and science-mapping analysis of research trends, hotspots, and future directions.
papers.authors: Chen H, He X, Chen Q
papers.abstract:
Acupoint injection therapy, including pharmacopuncture and bee-venom acupuncture (BVA), combines acupuncture-point stimulation with the local action of an injected substance. Despite growing clinical use, no bibliometric analysis has, to our knowledge, been dedicated to the broader acupoint-injection field. This study mapped its Web of Science (WoS)-indexed landscape.
Articles and reviews on acupoint injection were retrieved from the WoS Core Collection Science Citation Index Expanded with a multi-term topic search covering acupoint injection, pharmacopuncture, BVA, and related terms, and were screened for relevance after within-database de-duplication. Analyses used R bibliometrix (v5.2.1): productivity of countries (corresponding-author and document-level), institutions, authors (disambiguated) and journals; Bradford and Lotka's Laws; keyword co-occurrence; thematic mapping and evolution; and a human-only sensitivity analysis.
After screening, 440 documents (331 articles, 109 reviews) were analyzed; output grew to a complete-year maximum of 52 in 2025 (compound annual growth rate 2011-2025, 13.3%; sparse before 2011). By corresponding author, South Korea (229; 52.5%) and China (147; 33.7%) produced 86.2% of output, yet international co-authorship was low (10.6%). Kyung Hee University was the most productive institution (111 documents), and Ha In-Hyuk the most productive and most cited author (59 publications; local h-index 12). Medicine published the most documents (57). Leading author keywords were acupuncture (117), pharmacopuncture (89), and bee venom (70). Author productivity followed Lotka's Law (fitted exponent 1.77). A human-only sensitivity analysis showed Brazil's contribution fell from 27 to 1 (almost entirely veterinary aquapuncture). Thematic analysis identified a central pharmacopuncture-bee-venom-Korean-medicine theme.
Within the WoS-indexed literature, research on acupoint injection therapy is concentrated in South Korea and China, with BVA a prominent and highly cited sub-field and limited international collaboration. All impact indicators are corpus-based. These findings reflect the WoS-indexed landscape, not the entire global literature (which includes substantial regionally indexed output), and characterize research activity and structure rather than clinical efficacy, mechanism, or study quality.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture in myofascial pain: the role of the fascial structure. A case series.
papers.authors: Angiolini S, Gagliardi V, Lovato A, Ceccherelli F, Gagliardi G
papers.abstract: Electroacupuncture is a well-established practice in the treatment of a wide range of pathological conditions, including myofascial pain. In this context, the muscular fascia is attracting increasing research interest due to its role in the onset and maintenance of painful conditions. The myofascial system, as an anatomical and functional structure, can serve as a target for the treatment of patients suffering from myofascial pain, by addressing the structural and functional changes that occur at this level due to various pathophysiological causes. This study reports four cases in which electroacupuncture has been applied in the erector spinae fascia; Ultrasound guidance was used to precisely locate the target and the position of the needles. Two sets of two pairs of paravertebral needles were used in the interested segment (cervical, thoracic, lumbar) and stimulated at 10 Hz for 25 minutes. We report one case of a patient affected by cervical pain, two cases of patients suffering from thoracolumbar pain, and one case of a patient with cervical pain associated with a right C6-C7 disc herniation. All these patients have been successfully treated with fascial electroacupuncture in the erector spinae fascia. In this framework, fascial electroacupuncture led to the resolution of the myofascial pain syndrome. This demonstrates that the muscular fascia is not a simple and inert structure, but a complex tissue, whose alterations can compromise a patient's state of health.

papers.title: Effects of acupuncture on sleep and fatigue in older adults treated for chronic low back pain: Secondary analyses of the BackInAction randomized clinical trial.
papers.authors: Mu CX, Cook AJ, DeBar LL, Li V, Pressman A, Dean L et al.
papers.abstract:
Acupuncture can reduce back pain and chronic pain symptoms, while potentially reducing the need for pharmacological interventions in older adults with chronic low back pain (cLBP). This exploratory analysis examined the effects of acupuncture for cLBP on sleep and fatigue outcomes in older adults.
Using BackInAction trial data, we examined the effectiveness of standard acupuncture (SA: 8-15 sessions across 12 weeks) and enhanced acupuncture (EA: standard acupuncture plus 4-6 additional sessions) among 743 older adults with cLBP. We looked at sleep duration, sleep quality, and fatigue using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) compared to usual medical care (UMC). Linear regression with Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) was used to model the outcomes measured at 3, 6, and 12 months post-baseline except for sleep quality which was only measured at 6 months post-baseline.
Compared to UMC, participants in the EA arm reported lower fatigue at 12 months (Adjusted Mean Difference (AMD) [95% CI]:-2.28 [-3.59, 0.96]). There were no statistically significant differences in sleep quality or duration at any time point between any groups. Exploratory analyses revealed that among women, the EA arm reported lower fatigue at 12 months (AMD [95% CI]: -1.84 [-3.50, -0.18]). Women in EA reported better sleep quality (AMD [95% CI]: -2.08 [-3.89, -0.26]) and longer duration at 6 months relative to women in SA (AMD [95% CI]: 0.22 [0.02, 0.41]).
Acupuncture may reduce fatigue in older patients with cLBP, whereas the effects of acupuncture for cLBP on sleep outcomes remain limited.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture as an adjunctive treatment for non-dipper hypertension: study protocol for a multicentre, randomised, sham-controlled trial.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Lai SH, Hu WX, Zhang B, Zhang C, Lu L et al.
papers.abstract:
Blood pressure normally follows a circadian rhythm, with a 10%–20% nocturnal decline relative to daytime levels; a decline of <10% is defined as a non-dipper pattern and is associated with a higher risk of hypertension-related target-organ damage. Although long-acting antihypertensive medications can reduce nighttime blood pressure, their effectiveness remains limited. Electroacupuncture (EA), as an adjunctive therapy, may improve circadian blood pressure rhythms; however, evidence from large, multicentre trials remains insufficient and its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study, therefore, aims to further evaluate the efficacy of adjunctive EA for non-dipper hypertension and explore its potential mechanisms.
This multicentre, randomised, sham acupuncture-controlled, patient-blinded clinical trial will recruit 404 patients with non-dipper hypertension, who will be randomly assigned (1:1) to EA or sham SA three times weekly for 8 weeks, followed by a 3-month follow-up. The primary outcome is the proportion of participants converting from a non-dipper to a dipper blood pressure pattern at week 8. Secondary outcomes include nocturnal blood pressure decline, 24-hour mean blood pressure, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and 36-Item Short Form Health Survey scores. Exploratory metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses will be performed using serum and whole-blood samples collected at baseline and after treatment.
This study protocol (V.2.0, 20 December 2023) involves human participants and was approved by the ethics committee of the Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine (no. 2023NL-278-02). The study findings will be disseminated through presentations at scientific conferences and publications in peer-reviewed journals.
ITMCTR2025000815.

papers.title: Chuzhen Therapy- A Non-Invasive External Therapy of Traditional Chinese Medicine for Non-specific Low Back Pain.
papers.authors: Jiang L, Yang H, Liu Y, Dong Y, Feng C, Chen K et al.
papers.abstract: Low back pain (LBP) represents a prevalent and heterogeneous musculoskeletal disorder that severely impairs patients' daily functioning, with approximately 90%-95% of clinical cases categorized as non-specific low back pain (NSLBP). First-line conservative management for NSLBP predominantly relies on oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and opioid analgesics; however, these pharmacotherapies carry notable adverse risks, including peptic ulceration, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and long-term drug dependence. Accordingly, this study aimed to develop a safe, nonpharmacological alternative intervention for NSLBP. Chuzhen therapy, a distinctive external therapeutic modality originating from the Nine Needles described in the Huangdi Neijing (Yellow Emperor's Internal Classic), integrates core therapeutic principles of acupuncture and tuina without penetrating the skin. Unlike conventional tuina, which imposes heavy physical strain on practitioners and may result in inconsistent stimulation intensity among operators, Chuzhen therapy employs specialized, customized instruments to deliver stable, reproducible, and targeted acupoint stimulation with minimal physical exertion. Preclinical animal studies have validated its analgesic mechanisms, demonstrating that Chuzhen intervention elevates pain thresholds by modulating central monoamine neurotransmitter concentrations. This report establishes a fully standardized clinical protocol for Chuzhen therapy targeting NSLBP, covering standardized acupoint selection, pretreatment preparation, unified treatment duration, complete operational workflows, and standardized safety precautions. Three validated clinical outcome metrics-the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and Short Form-36 (SF-36) Health Survey-were adopted to preliminarily assess the feasibility and clinical applicability of the proposed protocol. Findings from this single-arm, self-controlled protocol-validation trial indicate that standardized Chuzhen therapy significantly alleviates pain intensity, restores lumbar physical function, and improves long-term health-related quality of life among patients with NSLBP. No serious adverse events were documented throughout the intervention period.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of a Supervised-to-Home Electro-Press Needling Intervention for Acute Postoperative Pain After Mandibular Third Molar Extraction: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial Protocol.
papers.authors: Jiang Y, Jin Q, Zhao T, Li R, Yuan R, Wang F et al.
papers.abstract:
Although acute pain after mandibular third molar extraction is usually self-limited, early recovery varies considerably among individuals, and some patients continue to experience clinically relevant pain despite standard analgesic management. This protocol evaluates a supervised-to-home electro-press needling intervention that combines a 30-minute post-extraction electrical stimulation session with retained hand-patch self-stimulation for up to 48 hours. The intervention is intended as an adjunct to, rather than a replacement for, standard postoperative analgesia.
A Phase I pragmatic randomized controlled trial (PRCT) was conducted to optimize the stimulation parameters. Sixty participants were allocated 1:1:1 to 3-Hz electro-press needling, 3/15-Hz electro-press needling, or a control condition. The optimized regimen is evaluated in this second-stage, single-center, participant-blinded, context-matched sham-controlled, superiority randomized trial, which will enroll 100 adults undergoing minimally invasive extraction of an impacted mandibular third molar. After prespecified stratification by surgical difficulty and completion of extraction, participants will be randomized 1:1 to electro-press needling or a nonpenetrating sham intervention. The sham procedure matches treatment context and initial sensory cues but is not assumed to be physiologically inert. The primary outcome is overall postoperative pain intensity at 48 hours, assessed using a continuous 10-cm Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). Serial VAS assessments will be obtained at 2, 4, and 6 hours, at 24 and 48 hours, and once daily on postoperative days 3-7. Secondary outcomes include rescue-analgesic use, oral health-related quality of life, adverse events, blinding success, and other prespecified patient-centered outcomes. The primary 48-hour VAS outcome will be analyzed using a linear model adjusted for surgical-difficulty stratum, while repeated VAS measurements will be analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model. The primary analysis will follow the intention-to-treat principle.
Following parameter optimization in a phase I PRCT, this protocol will estimate the short-term additional effect of a complete supervised-to-home electro-press needling strategy relative to a specified nonpenetrating sham comparator when both are delivered alongside standard postoperative care. Joint evaluation of pain intensity, rescue-analgesic requirements, patient-centered recovery, safety, and blinding will inform the design of subsequent trials without establishing the isolated effects of individual intervention components or routine clinical applicability.

papers.title: Bioactive constituents from Iris domestica attenuate OGD/R-induced PC12 cell injury by suppressing oxidative stress and mitochondrial apoptosis.
papers.authors: Cui L, Liu Y, Sun J, Hu Z, Jin L, Diao S et al.
papers.abstract:
Ischemic stroke (IS) causes neuronal injury involving oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Iris domestica (L.) Goldblatt & Mabb (Iridaceae), known as Shegan in traditional Chinese medicine, has potential neuroprotective properties; however, its structurally defined active constituents remain insufficiently characterized.
This study aimed to isolate secondary metabolites from I. domestica and evaluate their protective effects and potential mechanisms in an OGD/R-induced PC12 cell model.
Secondary metabolites were isolated from I. domestica by chromatographic techniques and identified by 1D/2D NMR, high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (HR-ESI-MS), and optical rotation. Neuroprotective activity was evaluated in oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-injured PC12 cells. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential, and apoptosis-related proteins were further assessed, and network pharmacology and molecular docking were performed.
Four previously undescribed compounds, irisdomeones A-C (1-3) and irisdomeoside F (4), with 21 known compounds (5-25), were isolated. Eleven compounds showed protective effects at 10 μM. Irisdomeone A (1) and belamchinoside D (24) exhibited the strongest activity and were further evaluated at 5 and 10 μM. Both reduced intracellular ROS accumulation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, increased the Bcl-2/Bax ratio, and decreased cleaved caspase-3 expression. Network pharmacology and molecular docking suggested involvement of HIF-1 signaling and mitochondrial apoptosis-related targets.
Irisdomeone A and belamchinoside D exhibited protective effects against OGD/R-induced PC12 cell injury, associated with reduced oxidative stress, attenuation of mitochondrial dysfunction, and inhibition of apoptosis. These findings identify compounds 1 and 24 as promising cytoprotective constituents in this in vitro model.

papers.title: Malaria burden and care in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon during the COVID-19 pandemic: A mixed-methods study.
papers.authors: Fernández SP, Rojas LM, Gómez J, Sandoval-Bances J, Condori-Catachura S, García PD et al.
papers.abstract:
The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with reported disruptions to healthcare delivery and malaria control activities in remote, malaria-endemic indigenous communities with limited access to healthcare. Such communities in the Peruvian Amazon may have been especially vulnerable due to interruptions in malaria surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment. We investigated malaria burden, healthcare access, and community perceptions during the COVID-19 pandemic in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Amazonas region of Peru.
A convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conducted in 2021 and 2022 across four indigenous communities in the Río Santiago district, Amazonas region, Peru. Quantitative data were collected through cross-sectional malaria surveys, and qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with inhabitants, community health workers, and local health personnel. Malaria was detected by microscopy and confirmed by PCR. Factors associated with PCR-confirmed malaria were analyzed using a generalized estimating equation (GEE) to account for repeated observations within participants across study years. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and both components were integrated using the Pillar Integration Process framework.
A total of 514 participants were included. PCR-based malaria prevalence was 17.6% in 2021 and 26.09% in 2022. P. falciparum prevalence was particularly high in the Alianza Progreso community (2021: 24.19%, 2022: 16.16%) compared to the other studied communities. Previous malaria and chills were associated with PCR-confirmed malaria. Qualitative findings indicated that COVID-19-related disruptions affected malaria control activities by interrupting diagnosis and treatment availability, reducing community follow-up, and prioritizing COVID-19 response activities over malaria control. Participants also described fear of COVID-19, temporary migration to farm areas, and reliance on herbal medicine during the pandemic.
The COVID-19 pandemic may have contributed to exacerbated pre-existing challenges to malaria control in remote indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon. Our findings document a substantial malaria burden, alongside participant-reported disruptions to malaria surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment. Strengthening malaria surveillance, ensuring continuity of diagnosis and treatment, and improving healthcare access in geographically isolated communities will be critical priorities for supporting malaria elimination efforts in Peru.

papers.title: Evaluating the accuracy of risk of bias assessment by one vs two independent reviewers: Part 3 of a meta-research study of rapid review methodological trade-offs.
papers.authors: Corso M, Ead L, Brunton G, Negrini S, Tricco AC, Côté P
papers.abstract:
To determine the accuracy of one versus two independent reviewers on the risk of bias (ROB) of randomized controlled trials in systematic reviews of acupuncture, education and transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) for chronic low back pain (LBP). Secondary objectives included measuring inter-rater reliability and describing ratings of signalling questions.
One reviewer assessed the ROB of relevant studies (acupuncture: 37, education: 16, TENS: 17) with the Neck and Back modified ROB1 tool as per the original reviews. Possible ratings were 'low', 'unclear' or 'high' and were compared to consensus ratings from the original reviews, grouping 'unclear' and 'high' ROB in our analysis, to calculate sensitivity, specificity, positive (PPV) and negative predictive values (NPV) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). . We calculated inter-rater reliability with Cohen's Kappa and 95% CIs and described differences in signalling questions. The sensitivity analysis assessed how grouping ROB overall ratings impacted outcomes.
The sensitivity and PPV of single reviewer ROB assessment in the acupuncture review were 50%, 95% CI [1, 99], and the specificity and NPV were 97%, 95% CI [85, 100]. Reasons for discrepancies included selective reporting, allocation concealment, patient and provider blinding, and co-interventions. We were unable to calculate sensitivity and PPV in the education and TENS reviews because all ratings were agreements. The specificity and NPV were 100%, 95% CI [79, 100] in the education review and 100%, 95% CI [80, 100] in the TENS review. Our sensitivity analysis showed grouping 'low' and 'unclear' studies reduced the specificity in all reviews, ranging from 57% to 79%. Inter-rater reliability across all overall ratings ranged from 0.22 to 0.35. Common signalling question discrepancies include provider blinding, intention-to-treat analysis, baseline similarities and selective reporting.
We suggest that ROB assessment in rapid reviews of chronic LBP should not be conducted by a single reviewer without verification. Using ROB thresholds to include or exclude studies in the synthesis may result in different results depending on the threshold selected. Critical methodological considerations for the validity and reliability include the review topic, tool selection, number of reviewers, and reviewer experience and training.
Systematic reviews include a risk of bias assessment of studies to determine the trustworthiness of results. This assessment is usually done by two independent reviewers, but rapid reviews can use only one reviewer to save time. We examined whether using one reviewer instead of two affects the accuracy of risk of bias ratings in systematic reviews of treatments for chronic low back pain. One reviewer assessed the risk of bias for studies included in three reviews of interventions for chronic low back pain (acupuncture, education and TENS). We used the same tool and instructions as the original reviews and compared the single reviewer's ratings with the final ratings from the original systematic reviews. We also measured how consistently reviewers agreed, which questions led to different ratings, and whether how the studies were grouped in the analysis changed the accuracy of one reviewer. For acupuncture, the single reviewer correctly rated low risk of bias studies half of the time (sensitivity: 50%) and correctly rated most studies as either 'unclear' or 'high' risk of bias (specificity: 97%). When the ratings were different, it was mainly related to the rating of selective reporting of results, treatment concealment, blinding and whether patients were allowed to have other treatments in the risk of bias tool. In the education and TENS reviews, the single reviewer correctly rated all studies as either 'unclear' or 'high' risk of bias. When we grouped 'low' and 'unclear' ROB ratings and compared them to 'high' ROB ratings to test whether how we grouped the ratings impacted the results, the single reviewer correctly rated fewer studies as 'unclear' or 'high' risk of bias (specificity ranging from 57% to 79%). When the overall ratings were different, it was related to the rating of questions in the risk of bias tool, including selective reporting of results, treatment concealment, blinding, whether analyses included all randomized participants, whether groups were similar at the start of the study and whether patients were allowed to have other treatments. Our findings suggest that risk of bias assessments should not be conducted by a single reviewer without a second reviewer checking the work because decisions about the quality of studies could affect the evidence used to draw conclusions about the effectiveness of interventions.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture-treated CUMS mice exhibit reduced depression-like behaviors and attenuated hippocampal synaptic abnormalities, accompanied by changes in Maf1-PTEN-AKT-mTORC1 signaling.
papers.authors: Zhang K, Zhao H, Gao Y, Ma W, Cai W, Zhang X et al.
papers.abstract:
Depression is associated with impaired hippocampal synaptic plasticity. We investigated the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) on depression-like behaviors and hippocampal synaptic alterations in chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mice, together with associated changes in Maf1-PTEN-AKT-mTORC1-related signaling.
Male C57BL/6 J mice underwent 6 weeks of CUMS. EA was administered at GV20 and GV29 from week 4 (2 Hz, 20 min/day, 3 weeks). Behavioral outcomes were assessed using the sucrose preference, forced swim, tail suspension, and open field tests. Hippocampal morphological and molecular alterations were examined using Nissl and Golgi staining, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, RT-qPCR, and ChIP-qPCR.
CUMS reduced sucrose preference and locomotor activity and increased immobility in the FST and TST; these alterations were attenuated in CUMS mice receiving the EA protocol compared with untreated CUMS mice. EA attenuated hippocampal histological abnormalities, increased dendritic spine density, and upregulated PSD-95, synaptophysin (SYN), MAP-2, and GAP-43. EA reduced Maf1 and PTEN protein levels and PTEN mRNA expression, while increasing AKT-mTORC1-related phosphorylation, including that of 4E-BP1 and p70S6K. Maf1 enrichment at the PTEN promoter was also reduced following EA treatment.
Compared with untreated CUMS mice, those receiving the complete EA protocol exhibited improved depression-like behavioral measures and attenuated hippocampal synaptic structural and molecular abnormalities, accompanied by changes in Maf1-PTEN-AKT-mTORC1-related signaling.

papers.title: Yiqi Jiedu formula suppresses nasopharyngeal carcinoma growth in association with glycerophospholipid metabolism remodeling: An integrated metabolomics and lipidomics study.
papers.authors: Zhou M, Wu Y, Chen S, Liang R, Lin T, Liu J et al.
papers.abstract:
Yiqi Jiedu formula (YQJDF), a classical traditional Chinese medicine prescription, has been used in the clinical management of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Although its therapeutic potential has been indicated by clinical experience, the molecular mechanisms through which it reprograms the intratumoral lipid metabolism remain uncharacterized.
This study aimed to systematically elucidate the antitumor mechanisms of YQJDF by profiling lipid metabolic alterations in tumor tissues through an integrated approach combining non-targeted metabolomics and lipidomics, and identify and validate the key enzymatic regulators of lipid metabolism modulated by the formula.
Non-targeted metabolomics was first performed to map globally altered metabolic pathways in tumor tissues. Subsequently, lipidomics was conducted, with exploratory differential lipids identified using a nominal P value < 0.05 and an OPLS-DA VIP score > 1, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Differential lipids were subjected to hierarchical clustering and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses. Molecular docking was employed to predict the binding affinity of major formula constituents to key enzymes in enriched pathways, and the expression of candidate targets was validated by immunohistochemistry (IHC).
Non-targeted metabolomics suggested that YQJDF may influence sphingolipid metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, and galactose metabolism. Lipidomics identified 597 exploratory differential lipids, with 179 upregulated and 418 downregulated, of which only PA(P-30:8_18:0), PG(20:4_22:5), and SM(t36:3) remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (FDR < 0.05 and VIP > 1). Clustering analysis showed that these differential lipids were concentrated in phospholipid subclasses. KEGG enrichment analysis pinpointed three core pathways: Choline metabolism in cancer, Efferocytosis, and Glycerophospholipid metabolism. The convergent findings from both omics platforms suggested glycerophospholipid metabolism as a potential pathway associated with treatment. Accordingly, molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities between key formula constituents and critical glycerophospholipid enzymes, including PGS1 and PLA2G4A. IHC showed lower PGS1 and PTDSS1 expression and higher PISD and PLA2G4A expression in the YQ and 3YQ groups compared with the control group. CEPT1 expression was significantly reduced only in the 3YQ group, with a non-significant downward trend in the YQ group.
YQJDF treatment showed antitumor effects and was accompanied by extensive lipid metabolic remodeling in NPC tissues. Glycerophospholipid metabolism may represent an important metabolic pathway associated with YQJDF treatment, and several lipid-metabolism-related enzymes were identified as molecular candidates for further mechanistic investigation. These findings provide a basis for further validation of the role of lipid metabolic alterations in the antitumor response to YQJDF.

papers.title: Non-hormonal management of menopause symptoms-the statement of the European Society of Gynecology.
papers.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
papers.authors: Castelo-Branco C, Kiesel L, Yoldemir T, Chabbert-Buffet N, Jakab A, Genazzani A et al.
papers.abstract:
Menopausal symptoms, particularly vasomotor symptoms (VMS), sleep disturbances, mood disorders, and genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM), affect a substantial proportion of women and may significantly impair the quality of life. Although menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) remains the most effective treatment, many women have contraindications to hormonal treatment or prefer non-hormonal options.
To review and provide evidence-based recommendations on current non-hormonal interventions for the management of menopausal symptoms.
The European Society of Gynecology convened an expert panel that performed a comprehensive literature review using MEDLINE and EMBASE. Clinical guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyzes, randomized controlled trials, and relevant primary studies evaluating non-hormonal interventions for menopausal symptoms were identified, critically appraised, and synthesized through a structured consensus process.
Lifestyle modification, including healthy diet, regular physical activity, weight control, sleep hygiene, and behavioral interventions, forms the foundation of menopausal care. Among pharmacological therapies, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, clonidine, oxybutynin, and pregabalin demonstrate varying degrees of efficacy for VMS. Neurokinin receptor antagonists, particularly fezolinetant and elinzanetant, represent the most effective evidence-based non-hormonal pharmacologic therapies currently available. Cognitive behavioral therapy and clinical hypnosis effectively reduce VMS-related distress and improve sleep and quality of life. Evidence for complementary approaches such as mindfulness, yoga, acupuncture, acupressure, reflexology, phytoestrogens, S-equol, DT56a, purified pollen extracts, and black cohosh ranges from moderate to limited. For GSM, lubricants, moisturizers, hyaluronic acid preparations, and pelvic floor muscle training provide symptomatic benefit, whereas current evidence does not support routine use of vaginal laser therapy.
Non-hormonal therapies provide effective and individualized treatment options for menopausal symptoms, particularly for women who are unable or unwilling to use MHT. Neurokinin receptor antagonists, selected pharmacologic agents, psychological interventions, and targeted GSM therapies represent the strongest evidence-based approaches currently available. The choice of treatment should consider symptom profile, contraindications, adverse effects, regulatory approval, and patient preferences.

papers.title: Therapeutic values of medicinal plants on inflammation indexes and the severity of pain in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review.
papers.authors: Ghorani-Azam A, Nazari-Khanamiri F, Sepahi S
papers.abstract:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disorder that is described as inflammation in the synovial tissues of joints, cartilages, bones, and less frequently in extra-articular localities, which affects the quality of life, especially in older population. Various medicinal plants and their bioactive compounds have demonstrated significant anti-inflammatory effects by modulating pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, as well as inhibiting NF-κB signaling pathways in rheumatoid arthritis. This review aimed to study the therapeutic values of some medicinal plants on inflammatory indexes in RA patients.
All electronic databases were searched for articles on November 2025 by searching "medicinal plant," and "Rheumatoid arthritis" as the key terms. After collecting the relevant documents, the data were extracted and described.
In total, data of 43 articles with 7523 included patients were extracted. Findings demonstrated that some medicinal plants are rich sources of active constituents, which can affect inflammatory factors such as levels of serum rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated protein antibodies, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein, that subsequently leads to improvement of visual analogue scale, disease activity score with 28-joint counts, health assessment questionnaire, joint count for pain.
Medicinal plants and herbal formulations are promising sources to replace or at least limit the excessive consumption of NSAIDs in RA diseases and associated comorbidities. Accordingly, appropriate herbal therapy may be helpful in treating the RA or minimizing the RA-associated symptoms.

papers.title: Bacterial profile, antimicrobial resistance, and predictors of mortality in necrotizing fasciitis: a multicentre prospective study in Uganda.
papers.authors: Ali AA, Vahwere BM, Abraha D, Kahie FD, Michael M, Hakizimana T et al.
papers.abstract:
Necrotizing fasciitis carries a high mortality burden in low-resource settings, yet data from Uganda are scarce. This study aimed to describe the bacterial profile, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and predictors of mortality among patients with necrotizing fasciitis in Uganda.
A prospective hospital-based study was conducted among patients with surgically confirmed necrotizing fasciitis at Mubende, Hoima, and Fort Portal Regional Referral Hospitals between April and August 2025. Wound swabs and tissue samples were cultured for bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and patients were followed until discharge or death. Modified Poisson regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality.
Among 64 patients (56.3% male), median age group was 13-18 years, most had Type I polymicrobial necrotizing fasciitis (60.9%), while Type II monomicrobial infections accounted for 29.7%. Streptococcus spp. (24.6%) and Staphylococcus spp. (20.2%) were the most common isolates. While Streptococcus spp. remained highly susceptible to Ceftriaxone (92.9%) and Clindamycin (96.4%), Staphylococcus spp. resistance to Ampicillin (73.9%), though retained sensitivity to Vancomycin (87.0%); Escherichia coli (18.4%) and Klebsiella spp. (14.9%) exhibited multi-drug resistance but remained largely susceptible to carbapenems (Imipenem/Meropenem, 95-100%) and Ciprofloxacin (> 90%). Anaerobes: Bacteroides and Clostridium spp were reported. Diabetes mellitus, prior use of herbal medicine, undernutrition, and anaerobic bacterial infection (all p < 0.05) despite anaerobes showing high sensitivity to Metronidazole (75-100%).
Necrotizing fasciitis carries high mortality in Uganda, with anaerobic infection, diabetes, herbal medicine use, and undernutrition as key predictors; empiric therapy in low-resource settings should include anaerobic coverage with metronidazole or clindamycin.

papers.title: Effects of electroacupuncture on acute lung injury induced by lipopolysaccharide in mice.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Xiao L, Liu J, Zeng W, Li X, Han Y, Liu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
The aim of this study was to evaluate the differences in mitogen-activated protein kinase/nuclear factor-κB (MAPF/NF-κB) signaling pathway activation and the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) at different traditional acupuncture point locations on acute lung injury (ALI) caused by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in mice.
Thirty-six male Kunming mice were randomly divided into six groups: the LU9 group, the LU9 + BL13 group, the ST36 group, the ST36 + BL13 group, the control group, and the untreated model group. Mice in the LU9, LU9 + BL13, ST36 and ST36 + BL13 groups received EA at the appropriate combination of LU9, ST36 and/or BL13 after intratracheal instillation of LPS (5 mg/kg). After the intervention, hematologic parameters were measured, histopathological changes in lung tissue were observed, and mRNA expression of interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, IL-10 and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and protein expression of NF-κB, phosphorylated(p)-p65/p65, p-IκBα/IκBα (inhibitor of NF-κB), MAPK p-p38/p38 and MAPK p-Erk/Erk (extracellular signal-regulated kinase) in lung tissue were detected.
EA ameliorated lung injury scores in LPS-stimulated mice. In addition, EA reduced the activation of NF-κB p65 and mRNA expression of IL-1β and TNF-α in lung tissue. Furthermore, EA at LU9 or LU9 + BL13 increased the number of leukocytes in the blood and the mRNA expression of IL-10 in pulmonary tissue and also inhibited the phosphorylation of IκBα in pulmonary tissue. EA at ST36 or ST36 + BL13 inhibited mRNA expression of IL-6 and phosphorylation of MAPK p38.
EA at LU9, ST36 and BL13 effectively alleviated lung tissue inflammation in mice with LPS-induced acute lung injury. The anti-inflammatory mechanisms differed between EA at LU9 and EA at ST36.

papers.title: Association of Nonpharmacologic Therapies with Health-Related Quality-of-Life Outcomes in Patients with Chronic Low Back Pain: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
papers.authors: Licciardone JC, Gallo CE, Nishino S, Koch AT, Richards KB, Agubuzo DN et al.
papers.abstract:
Nonpharmacologic therapies (NPTs) are recommended as first-line treatment for chronic low back pain (CLBP).
A retrospective cohort study was conducted within a national pain research registry from April 2016 through April 2025. Patients with CLBP reported use of exercise therapy, yoga, massage therapy, spinal manipulation, and acupuncture at enrollment and at quarterly intervals through 12 months. Health-related quality-of-life (HRQOL) outcomes for physical function, anxiety, depression, fatigue, sleep disturbance, participation in social roles, and pain interference were collected at enrollment and quarterly intervals. Generalized estimating equations were used to measure HRQOL outcomes associated with each NPT and a series of potential confounders. The magnitude of the standardized mean difference (SMD) between users and nonusers of each NPT was used to assess the clinical importance of the results.
A total of 723 (40.4%) of 1789 study patients used at least one NPT at enrollment. Exercise therapy was associated with less fatigue (SMD, 0.06) and sleep disturbance (SMD, 0.07), and yoga was associated with better physical function (SMD, 0.06) and greater participation in social roles (0.06) over 12 months. None of these results approached the threshold for clinical importance. Users of massage therapy, spinal manipulation, and acupuncture did not report better outcomes than nonusers on any HRQOL measure. In multivariable analyses, greater pain self-efficacy was consistently associated with better outcomes across all HRQOL measures, whereas greater pain catastrophizing was often associated with worse outcomes.
None of the NPTs for CLBP yielded clinically important differences between users and nonusers over 12 months. These findings have important clinical implications in the management of CLBP because each studied NPT is recommended in major clinical practice guidelines and commonly used by patients.

papers.title: Acupuncture for Perioperative Pain Management in Cesarean Section: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Focusing on Pain Subtypes and Heterogeneity Exploration.
papers.authors: Xu R, Chen T, Zhang L, Chen M
papers.abstract:
Cesarean section (CS) is among the most common surgical procedures worldwide, yet postoperative pain management remains challenging, with opioid-related adverse effects constraining analgesic options in lactating women.
To systematically evaluate the efficacy of acupuncture and acupoint stimulation for perioperative pain management in CS, focusing on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)-classified pain subtypes and heterogeneity sources.
We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and CBM through January 15, 2025 (PROSPERO: CRD42023487558). Eligible studies were RCTs evaluating acupuncture for CS perioperative pain. Primary outcomes were 24-h and 48-h pain intensity and analgesic consumption. Fixed- or random-effects models were used according to the heterogeneity criteria described in the Methods. Heterogeneity was explored via meta-regression, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses. Certainty was assessed using GRADE.
Forty-one RCTs (n = 4,823) were included. Acupuncture and acupoint stimulation significantly reduced 24-hour pain (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -2.63, 95% CI [-2.97, -2.28]; prediction interval [-4.80, -0.46]; I² = 94%) and 48-hour pain (MD = -2.06, 95% CI [-2.29, -1.82]; I² = 96%). Low-RoB sensitivity analysis yielded SMD = -1.42, suggesting unblinded designs inflate estimates. Combined modalities produced the largest effect (SMD = -2.75). GRADE certainty was low-to-moderate across outcomes.
Acupuncture and acupoint stimulation may reduce pain after cesarean section. Substantial heterogeneity, risk of bias and low-to-moderate certainty limit confidence in the magnitude and applicability of the pooled effects. Use as an adjunct in enhanced recovery pathways warrants evaluation in rigorously designed trials.

papers.title: Best Evidence summary for Managing Insulin Injection-Related Lipohypertrophy: An International and Contextualized Synthesis.
papers.authors: Xie T, Cao C, Li Z, Liu X, Wang Y, Liu W
papers.abstract: We collated current best available evidence on the clinical management of injection-site lipohypertrophy (LH) in individuals with diabetes, supplying healthcare professionals with a resource for LH prevention and intervention. Guided by the 6S evidence pyramid, we conducted searches across both Chinese and international evidence-based resource databases, professional bodies, guideline portals, and bibliographic databases. Two dually trained reviewers (methodology and diabetology) independently extracted and synthesized the evidence, and generated a best available evidence set after quality appraisal, the evidence was graded using the JBI 2014 levels of evidence and grades of recommendation. In accordance with JBI recommendations and considering the FAME attributes of the evidence (feasibility, appropriateness, meaningfulness, and effectiveness), the recommendation levels were categorized as Grade A (strong recommendation) and Grade B (weak recommendation). Following the screening process, 21 documents were deemed eligible for inclusion: two clinical decision summaries, five guidelines, six expert consensus statements, six systematic reviews, and two randomized controlled trials. Twenty-four evidence statements were identified across six themes: assessment timing, screening methods, risk factors, prevention, management, and health education. Notably, given the widespread use of appropriate traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) techniques in LH management practice in China, the synthesized evidence also covered TCM-based measures, including moxibustion and herbal external application. The evidence collated in this investigation can serve as a practical touchstone for medical practitioners, patients, and families tasked with managing and forestalling LH linked to insulin therapy. However, in practice, appropriate evidence should be selected and applied, with full consideration of real-world contexts and individual differences. It should be noted that, because high-quality evidence is currently lacking in some areas, we included certain lower-quality studies after conducting rigorous searches and quality appraisals. The limitations of this evidence are identified in the evidence summaries, and routine use is not recommended without further evaluation. Clinicians should apply such evidence cautiously, with consideration of individual patient circumstances and informed consent.

papers.title: Integrated Management of Myofascial Pain Syndrome with Acupuncture, Tuina, and Rehabilitation: A Narrative Review.
papers.authors: Yu M, Zhang S, Li H, Li H, Qi W, Guo M
papers.abstract: Myofascial pain syndrome, MPS, is a prevalent musculoskeletal pain condition characterized by myofascial trigger points, MTrPs, local tenderness, referred pain, restricted range of motion, and functional impairment. Its clinical presentation may involve interacting tissue, neuromuscular, and pain-processing abnormalities, providing a rationale for multimodal management. This narrative review examines the pathophysiological basis of MPS and the potential complementary roles of acupuncture, Tuina, and rehabilitation, while distinguishing clinical findings from proposed mechanisms. Acupuncture may reduce pain and MTrP-related sensitivity through local and neurophysiological effects. Tuina may help relieve perceived stiffness and improve movement tolerance, whereas rehabilitation addresses mobility, strength, motor control, and self-management. We propose an "analgesia-release-retraining-maintenance" conceptual framework to organize these approaches according to the dominant clinical problems and treatment tolerance. The phases are intended as overlapping therapeutic priorities rather than mandatory sequential steps, with education and tolerable active rehabilitation incorporated throughout care. This author-proposed framework has not been prospectively validated, and its optimal sequencing and superiority over individual modalities or alternative multimodal strategies have not been established. It therefore offers a structure for clinical reasoning rather than a validated treatment algorithm. Future studies should evaluate patient selection, intervention dosage, treatment sequencing, safety, and comparative outcomes. Sustained functional recovery and reduced recurrence remain intended goals requiring clinical evaluation.

papers.title: Glymphatic dysfunction and amyloid-β clearance in Alzheimer's disease: mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential of traditional Chinese medicine.
papers.authors: Wang B, Luo L, Ying C, Yang J, Zhang Y
papers.abstract: The glymphatic system supports cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid (CSF-ISF) exchange and extracellular solute transport, and its dysfunction may contribute to amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation in Alzheimer's disease (AD). This narrative review examines mechanisms linking impaired brain fluid transport to Aβ retention, focusing on altered perivascular aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarization, vascular and paravascular remodeling, impaired cerebrovascular dynamics, astrocyte dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and sleep and circadian disturbances. It also evaluates preclinical evidence for Chinese herbal interventions. Preclinical studies have reported changes in CSF tracer influx or distribution, parenchymal solute efflux, meningeal lymphatic tracer transport, AQP4 localization, and lymphatic vessel morphology, often accompanied by reduced Aβ burden and improved cognitive performance. Other studies primarily report changes in cellular Aβ handling, inflammation, or sleep and therefore provide only indirect support for glymphatic involvement. Glymphatic exchange, intramural periarterial drainage, and meningeal lymphatic outflow are anatomically distinct processes with different experimental readouts; reduced tissue Aβ alone does not establish enhanced clearance. Major limitations include heterogeneity in experimental models and tracer methods, limited pathway-specific causal validation, and a lack of clinical evidence directly supporting these mechanisms of action. Dynamic transport measurements, pathway-specific perturbations, and standardized formulations are needed to determine whether enhancement of brain fluid and solute clearance represents a clinically translatable mechanism of Chinese herbal interventions in AD.

papers.title: ASTRO study: acupuncture sets of trial reported core outcomes for women's health across the lifespan.
papers.authors: Levett KM, Buay VC, Citkovitz C, Lumiere K, Schnyer R, Graca S et al.
papers.abstract:
Clinical trials of acupuncture are difficult to meaningfully aggregate due to small sample sizes and reductionist, heterogeneous outcome measures. To improve the quality of evidence, standardised reporting of minimum data that reflects whole-person health, essential to East Asian Medicine (EAM), is needed. The Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) initiative offers a methodology for developing core outcome sets (COS) through collaborative group consensus, including consumers. This study presents the 'Acupuncture Sets of Trial Reported Outcomes' (ASTRO) for women's health. Using domains of pain, sleep, mood/cognition and safety, the ASTRO framework captures EAM complexity as well as standardising reporting outcomes.
To develop a COS for acupuncture trials in women's health, reflecting whole-person health outcomes across the lifespan.
We used a COMET-informed three-stage consensus process involving practitioners, researchers, patients and policymakers to develop a COS for reporting minimum data for acupuncture trials in women's health. This process involved a systematic review, roundtable discussion, two-round Delphi survey and a consensus meeting. We examined the conditions of menstrual health, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, fertility, pregnancy and menopause to develop an outcome set for safety, feasibility and EAM specific outcomes.
From 320 studies, 579 outcomes were identified for the survey items and 319 respondents participated in two Delphi survey rounds. The attrition rate was 52% between surveys and respondents were mainly from English-speaking countries. A final COS of 12 outcomes was agreed on:Safety (n=2): serious adverse events and minor adverse events.EAM (n=8): primary and secondary patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), patient experience/satisfaction, EAM diagnostic indices (eg, tongue and pulse), demographics and changes in pain, sleep and mood/cognition.Feasibility (n=2): acceptability and cost.
The ASTRO Women's Health COS enables consistent, whole-person outcome reporting to improve the quality and comparability of acupuncture research.

papers.title: Staged integrative traditional Korean medicine for physiological resilience recovery in a frail postoperative older adult with sarcopenia: a case report.
papers.authors: Kim MJ, Kim JH, Oh SY, Kim MH
papers.abstract: Postoperative acute frailty and sarcopenia compromise functional recovery in older adults, often driven by gastrointestinal dysfunction accelerating muscle wasting through impaired nutrient absorption. While megestrol acetate (MA) is commonly used for postoperative anorexia, preventing metabolic rebound during withdrawal is challenging. This report demonstrates a staged integrative traditional Korean medicine approach managing MA discontinuation and postoperative sarcopenia. Coordinating herbal medicines with conventional care ensured a transition from MA while promoting muscle preservation and functional recovery. This framework mitigates medication-related risks and addresses acute frailty in postoperative older adults. A 79-year-old male presented with generalized weakness, orthostatic dizziness, and inability to ambulate unassisted following benign prostatic hyperplasia surgery and prolonged hospitalization for gastrointestinal bleeding and enteritis. Upon admission, he showed impaired functional metrics: Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score of 3, Korean Activities of Daily Living (K-ADL) score of 14, and appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM) of 6.58 kg/m². A three-stage traditional Korean medicine intervention (herbal medicines, intravenous hydration, acupuncture, cupping) was administered over 16 days. Stage 1 prioritized gut stabilization using Samryeongbaekchulsan and Insamyangyeong-tang alongside MA to enhance nutrient absorption. This improved total protein (6.3 to 7.1 g/dL), albumin (3.5 to 4.0g/dL), and normalized C-reactive protein (1.50 to 0.11 mg/dL), achieving independent ambulation (SPPB 8). Following MA discontinuation, he experienced transient rebound anorexia and dehydration. To manage this, Stages 2 (Recovery/Deprescribing) and 3 (Metabolic Stabilization) utilized tailored herbal medicines (Palmul-tang-gami A/B, Saengmaek-san) and intravenous hydration. This mitigated withdrawal stress, preserving skeletal muscle mass (22.5 to 22.7 kg) and maintaining functional recovery at discharge (SPPB 6, K-ADL 13). Additionally, heart rate variability parameters (total power, LF/HF ratio) closely mirrored the clinical trajectory, demonstrating utility in monitoring autonomic homeostatic reserve. In conclusion, coordinating herbal medicine with conventional supportive care restored physiological resilience in apostoperative older patient. This integrative model functions as a physiological bridge during MA deprescribing, providing a safe framework for complex geriatric management.

papers.title: Qishen Yangxin Granule ameliorates cardiac function and ventricular remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy by attenuating inflammation and myocardial fibrosis.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.authors: Tao S, Yu L, Li J, Zhang Z, Liu Y, Wu J et al.
papers.abstract:
Qishen Yangxin Granule (QSYX), a clinically utilized traditional Chinese medicinal formula, has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for cardiovascular diseases. However, its cardioprotective mechanism in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains incompletely defined.
To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of QSYX against DCM and the associated anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic mechanisms.
Cardioprotective effects of QSYX were assessed both in vivo using a doxorubicin-induced DCM rat model and in vitro using rat cardiac fibroblasts stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. Evaluations included cardiac function, histopathological analysis, levels of inflammatory factors, and myocardial fibrosis markers. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to explore the potential mechanism of QSYX-mediated improvement in cardiac structure and function. Modulation of the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway was examined via western blot, immunohistochemistry, confocal laser scanning microscope, and real-time reverse transcription-PCR. The specific p38 MAPK agonist LY188011 was used to verify the dependence of QSYX effect on the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.
QSYX administration improved cardiac function in DCM rats, accompanied by significant attenuation of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, apoptosis, inflammatory cell infiltration, and collagen deposition. Comparable protective effects were observed in lipopolysaccharide-treated cardiac fibroblasts. Mechanistically, QSYX suppressed lipopolysaccharide-induced upregulation of TLR4, p38 MAPK, and NF-κB p65 and downregulated the expression of inflammatory factors and myocardial fibrosis markers. Furthermore, intervention with LY188011 confirmed that the cardioprotective effects of QSYX are mediated through suppression of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.
QSYX attenuates myocardial inflammation and fibrosis primarily through inhibition of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby exerting cardioprotective effects against DCM-induced cardiac injury.

papers.title: Thermosensitive in situ nasal gel of Magnoliae Flos-Centipeda Herba for allergic rhinitis: preparation, characterization, and in vivo pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics studies.
papers.authors: Ma Y, Wang Z, Kang B, Xia Q, Yan H
papers.abstract: Magnoliae Flos and Centipeda Herba are classic herbal medicines for allergic rhinitis in traditional Chinese medicine, yet conventional nasal drops suffer from rapid clearance by nasal mucocilia, leading to limited nasal residence time. Herein, a thermosensitive in situ gel loaded with Magnoliae Flos and Centipeda Herba extract (MFCH-TGL) was fabricated to achieve prolonged, safe intranasal delivery. The gel matrix was composed of 17% (w/v) poloxamer 407 and 1% (w/v) poloxamer 188, incorporated with 2.3% (w/v) alcoholic extract and 0.5% (v/v) volatile oil of MFCH. We systematically characterized sol-gel transition performance, rheological behavior, in vitro release and ex vivo nasal permeation, and further assessed anti-allergic pharmacodynamics in BALB/c mice as well as nasal pharmacokinetics in SD rats. The formulation exhibited a sol-gel transition at 33.5 °C within 17 s, with 40.6 ± 1.97% cumulative nasal permeation over 8 h. Medium-dose MFCH-TGL markedly reduced OVA-specific IgE (8.28 ± 1.64, P < 0.01) compared with the allergic model group (12.55 ± 1.86). Moreover, the gel displayed 1.46-fold longer half-life and 1.52-fold longer mean residence time than the MFCH aqueous solution. This thermosensitive in situ gel presents promising intranasal application potential, offering a feasible formulation strategy for traditional Chinese medicine against allergic rhinitis.

papers.title: Antioxidant and antiproliferative effects of flavonoid fractions from Citri Exocarpium Rubrum on A549 lung cancer cells and their underlying mechanisms by network pharmacology.
papers.authors: Wang J, Zeng S, Lu H, Chen Y, Wei M, Zeng G
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, with chemotherapy resistance limiting treatment efficacy. Citri Exocarpium Rubrum (CER), a flavonoid-rich traditional Chinese medicine, exhibits anticancer potential. This study investigated its antioxidant and antiproliferative effects against A549 lung cancer cells and the underlying mechanisms. Flavonoids were extracted from CER and partitioned into ethyl acetate and n-butanol fractions. Antioxidant capacity and antiproliferative effects were assessed by 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical and 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assays, respectively. Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and apoptosis were measured. Network pharmacology was conducted using TCMSP, SwissTargetPrediction and GeneCards, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Both fractions showed concentration-dependent DPPH radical scavenging (73.66% and 84.36% at 32 μg/mL) and inhibited A549 proliferation. The n-butanol fraction induced dose-dependent apoptosis with reduced MMP. Network pharmacology identified 6 active components, 255 targets, 5 hub targets (SRC, ESR1, BCL2, HSP90AA1, PPARG) and 20 enriched pathways related to cancer and calcium signalling. CER flavonoid fractions demonstrate antioxidant and antiproliferative activities against A549 cells via multi-component, multi-target mechanisms, supporting its potential clinical application in lung cancer therapy.

papers.title: Non-pharmacological fatigue management strategies in neurodegenerative conditions: a scoping review.
papers.authors: Alageel S, Hibberd J, Deane KHO
papers.abstract:
Fatigue is a common and disabling symptom across several neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease. Non-pharmacological strategies are widely used in clinical practice to address fatigue, yet the extent to which evidence from one neurodegenerative condition can inform fatigue management in others remains uncertain, particularly for Parkinson's disease where intervention trials are scarce.
To map the quantitative evidence on non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in adults with neurodegenerative diseases (excluding dementias), and to identify potentially transferable strategies, gaps, and priorities for research and practice, with particular relevance to Parkinson's disease.
Scoping review conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported using the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF; DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/MJEYP).
MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, AMED, and PsycINFO were searched for records published from January 2006 to 15 February 2025. Reference lists of relevant reviews and included studies were screened. Publications in English or Arabic were eligible.
Quantitative interventional studies, mixed-methods studies with extractable quantitative fatigue outcomes, and systematic reviews/meta-analyses evaluating non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in adults with progressive neurodegenerative conditions were eligible. Conditions of interest included multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, motor neurone disease, Huntington's disease, hereditary ataxias, multiple system atrophy, and progressive supranuclear palsy. Studies focusing solely on pharmacological, surgical, herbal, or homeopathic interventions, qualitative-only studies, and studies in dementias were excluded.
A bespoke charting form captured study design, population, intervention, comparator, delivery format, fatigue measures, and key findings. Studies were grouped by intervention type: exercise, psychological, educational, and complementary interventions. Systematic reviews/meta-analyses and primary intervention studies were synthesized as distinct evidence levels and were not combined quantitatively.
The search identified 12,618 records. After removal of 5,399 duplicates, 7,219 records were screened and 517 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility. Twenty-seven sources met the inclusion criteria: seven systematic reviews/meta-analyses, 16 randomized controlled trials, one non-randomized controlled study, and three uncontrolled pre-post studies. Evidence was dominated by multiple sclerosis, with only two small trials in Parkinson's disease and no fatigue-focused intervention trials in other progressive neurodegenerative conditions. The most consistent between-group benefits were observed for structured exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy, and educational/self-management programs in multiple sclerosis. Complementary interventions included acupuncture, light therapy, dietary interventions, and electrical stimulation; evidence across these approaches was mixed. Heterogeneity in intervention type, intensity, duration, supervision and delivery format, follow-up duration, and fatigue outcome measures limited direct comparison across studies.
Non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in neurodegenerative disease are most developed in multiple sclerosis, where structured exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy, and educational/self-management approaches show the most consistent benefit. Evidence for Parkinson's disease is sparse, and no fatigue-focused intervention trials were identified in other progressive neurodegenerative conditions. Future work should prioritize condition-specific feasibility and effectiveness studies, harmonized fatigue outcome sets, objective fatigability measures alongside patient-reported fatigue, and multimodal programs with clearly specified therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Acupoint Thread Embedding for Weight Loss in Women With Overweight or Obesity : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Xu S, Yang G, Hu C, Li X, Yin X, Zhao Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Whether acupoint thread embedding (ATE), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention, produces weight reduction remains uncertain.
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of ATE for weight reduction in women with overweight or obesity.
Randomized, sham-controlled trial masked to participants, outcome assessors, and analysts. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06316310).
Acupuncture Department, Shanghai Municipal Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.
132 women aged 18 to 45 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 24.0 kg/m2 or greater.
Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to ATE (6 sessions over 12 weeks) or sham ATE (superficial needle insertion at the same acupoints without manipulation, de qi, thread placement, or needle retention), followed by a 12-week follow-up.
The primary outcome was change in BMI from baseline to week 12, analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle using linear mixed-effects models.
At week 12, BMI and body weight decreased 0.7 kg/m2 (95% CI, -1.0 to -0.3 kg/m2) and 1.8 kg (CI, -2.7 to -0.9 kg), respectively, more with ATE than with sham ATE; at week 24, differences were -1.1 kg/m2 (CI, -1.7 to -0.6 kg/m2) and -3.0 kg (CI, -4.5 to -1.6 kg), respectively. Weight reduction of 5% or more occurred in 25.8% versus 9.1% (risk difference, 16.7 percentage points [CI, 3.7 to 29.3 percentage points]) at 12 weeks. Acupoint thread embedding produced greater reductions in waist and hip circumference, body fat percentage, and appetite scores, whereas cardiometabolic and patient-reported outcomes did not differ. Adverse events were mild and comparably distributed.
Single center, generally healthy women of reproductive age, unmasked acupuncturists, short-term follow-up, and underpowered for uncommon adverse events and subgroup analyses.
Acupoint thread embedding produced modest but sustained reductions in BMI and adiposity-related measures in Chinese women of reproductive age with overweight or obesity.
National Facility for Translational Medicine (Shanghai).

papers.title: Targeting the pyroptosis network: Research progress of natural products in intervention for acute lung injury.
papers.authors: Luo C, Tan J, Ning B, Ye Y, Tang Q, Jiang Z et al.
papers.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a serious clinical condition with high morbidity and mortality rates. Current ALI treatments have limitations. Natural products from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exhibit multi-component, multi-target and multi-pathway regulatory properties with good safety, making them promising candidates for ALI treatment. This review systematically summarizes the activation pathways of pyroptosis, its molecular regulatory network in ALI and the mechanisms by which natural products regulate pyroptosis to inhibit ALI progression. A 'natural products-pyroptosis-ALI' axis conceptual framework is proposed to provide theoretical support for clinical translation. Systematic literature searches were conducted on CNKI, Web of Science and PubMed up to March 2026, using keywords related to natural products, ALI and pyroptosis. This review covers TCM herbs, natural small-molecule compounds and TCM formulas that modulate pyroptosis to alleviate ALI, with all animal experiments adhering to ethical and international standards. Various natural products and TCM formulae effectively target pyroptosis, inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, Caspase-1 activation and Gasdermin D pore formation, thereby reducing IL-1β/IL-18 release, alleviating inflammatory cascades, protecting alveolar-capillary barrier integrity and mitigating oxidative stress. Activated pyroptosis further disturbs mitophagy, triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, engages the gut-lung axis, modulates epigenetic reprogramming and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition to amplify ALI. This review fills gaps in the systematic characterization of pyroptosis-ALI relationships and natural product-based therapies, aiming to expand ALI treatment options and advance ALI therapeutic development.
