papers.title: Clinical outcomes of Thunder-fire moxibustion with or without Yiqi Wenyang Tincture for cancer-related fatigue: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.authors: Liu P, Du X, Li H, Zhao J, Zhong Y, Peng Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a debilitating symptom with limited treatment options. This study evaluated whether thunder-fire moxibustion (TFM) combined with Yiqi Wenyang Tincture (YWT) could provide additional benefit for CRF beyond conventional integrative management (control).
In a three-arm randomized controlled trial, 255 cancer patients were allocated (85 per group) to TFM alone, TFM plus YWT (TFM + YWT), or conventional integrative management (control). The primary outcomes were the Revised Piper Fatigue Scale (PFS-R) total score and EORTC QLQ-C30 global quality-of-life score at week 6.
In conservative intention-to-treat analyses using baseline observation carried forward for five missing week-6 assessments, with ANCOVA adjusted for baseline score and HC3 robust standard errors, TFM + YWT had lower PFS-R scores than TFM alone (adjusted mean difference, -0.459; 95% CI, -0.793 to -0.126; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.021) and higher global quality of life (2.552; 0.589 to 4.515; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.033). Exploratory outcomes were analyzed in the complete-case set.
TFM, particularly when combined with YWT, may provide incremental clinical benefit for CRF; confirmation in larger trials with matched attention controls and longer follow-up is warranted. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2200063288, and International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR), ChiMCTR2200006558; registered on September 3, 2022.

papers.title: Huanglian Jiedu Decoction: An Ethnopharmacological Perspective on Molecular Mechanisms and Clinical Applications in Inflammatory Diseases.
papers.authors: Li G, Liu Y, Li Q, Yang K, Wang Z, Wang L et al.
papers.abstract:
Huanglian Jiedu Decoction (HLJDD) is a classic traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) renowned for its heat-clearing and detoxifying effects. For centuries, this formula has been widely used under the guidance of TCM theory to treat various inflammatory disorders characterized as "heat toxin" or "excess fire in the three burners." TCM considers "heat toxin" to be a common pathological mechanism underlying many inflammatory diseases, with clinical manifestations functionally analogous and corresponding to the infectious and non-infectious inflammation defined by modern Western medicine, rather than being strictly equivalent. Therefore, the traditional effects of HLJDD in clearing heat, purging fire, detoxifying, and cooling the blood provide a unique TCM theoretical foundation and alternative intervention strategy for the treatment of modern inflammatory diseases.
This review aims to systematically summarize the components, traditional efficacy, main active ingredients of HLJDD in inflammatory diseases, as well as its modern pharmacological effects and molecular mechanisms. By integrating traditional experience with modern scientific evidence, we strive to provide a solid scientific basis and translational strategies for the ethnomedicinal applications of this herbal medicine and its modern use in the prevention and treatment of inflammatory diseases.
A narrative literature search was performed in PubMed and CNKI from database inception to December 31, 2025, using "Huanglian Jiedu Decoction", "HLJDD", "anti-inflammatory", "inflammation" and their synonyms. Original research articles on the phytochemistry, network pharmacology, mechanisms, or clinical applications of HLJDD or its constituent herbs in inflammatory diseases were included; reviews, case reports, non-English/Chinese publications, and duplicates were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts, with disagreements resolved by consensus. A three-tier evidence classification (whole formula / single herb / pure compound) was applied to mechanistic studies, and findings were synthesized narratively given substantial heterogeneity. Only PubMed and CNKI were searched, which may limit comprehensiveness.
The anti-inflammatory activity of HLJDD is mainly attributed to its various alkaloids and flavonoid compounds. These components exert synergistic effects through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms, significantly inhibiting the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) and effectively regulating the activation of key inflammatory signaling pathways (such as NF-κB, MAPK, JAK-STAT, and the NLRP3 inflammasome). Both in vivo and in vitro experiments have confirmed that HLJDD exhibits significant anti-inflammatory and tissue-protective effects in various inflammatory disease models, including sepsis, acute lung injury, colitis, and skin inflammation. Its mechanism of action is characterized by a typical "multi-component, multi-target, multi-pathway" network regulation feature.
What is established is that HLJDD and its constituent compounds modulate the NF-κB, MAPK, JAK-STAT, and NLRP3 pathways in cellular and animal systems, although most mechanistic evidence derives from isolated compounds rather than the whole formula. What is suggestive is that HLJDD-containing interventions may confer clinical benefit in selected inflammatory conditions; however, current clinical evidence remains of very low certainty, as most reported studies are small-sample, non-blinded trials using modified formulas or combination therapies rather than the classic HLJDD formula alone. What remains hypothetical is whether these preclinical mechanisms translate into clinically meaningful efficacy in humans. Future research should therefore prioritize: in-depth mechanistic studies that rigorously distinguish whole-formula from compound-level evidence; standardized extraction and quality-control systems; delivery systems to improve bioavailability; and large-scale, rigorously designed randomized controlled trials-so that HLJDD may progressively advance from empirical use toward a safe and effective evidence-based anti-inflammatory therapy..

papers.title: Acupuncture alleviates post-stroke depression by inhibiting proline-driven ferroptosis in hippocampal neurons.
papers.authors: Sun P, Zou L, Li N, Liu H, Sun M, Xie J et al.
papers.abstract:
Post-stroke depression (PSD) represents a prevalent stroke complication with scarce therapeutic interventions. Acupuncture has shown clinical efficacy in PSD, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates whether acupuncture alleviates PSD by regulating proline metabolism-mediated ferroptosis.
We generated a rat PSD model via common carotid artery ligation coupled with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Acupuncture at GV20, GV26, GV24, and GV14 was administered for four weeks. Behavioral tests, TTC and Nissl staining, ELISA, qPCR, western blot, amino acid metabolomics, and hippocampal neuron cultures with proline intervention were performed.
Acupuncture robustly rescued depression-like phenotypes and mitigated hippocampal neuronal injury in PSD rats. Acupuncture decreased serum levels of iron ions, malondialdehyde (MDA) and reactive oxygen species (ROS), increased glutathione (GSH), and reversed the aberrant expression of ferroptosis-related proteins (GPX4, SLC7A11, ACSL4, TFR1) in the hippocampus. Amino acid metabolomics revealed elevated serum proline in PSD rats, which was normalized by acupuncture. Exogenous proline administration aggravated depressive behaviors and hippocampal ferroptosis. In cultured hippocampal neurons, high-dose proline directly induced ferroptosis and reduced cell viability.
Acupuncture ameliorates PSD by inhibiting hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis through regulation of proline metabolism, revealing a novel mechanism for acupuncture treatment.

papers.title: Acupuncture versus conventional therapy for painful temporomandibular disorders in women: a study protocol for an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.authors: Citó EBC, Coutinho BD, de Moraes MEA, Vale ML, Gondim DV
papers.abstract:
The prevalence of temporomandibular disorder (TMD) has been increasing, and its high rate of chronicity makes it a relevant public health concern. Despite the availability of several treatment options, there is still no consensus regarding the most effective approach for managing painful TMD.
This study presents the protocol for an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the effectiveness of acupuncture compared with conventional treatment in patients with painful TMD.
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) systemic individualized acupuncture based on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis; (2) local acupuncture according to Western diagnostic criteria; or (3) standard treatment consisting of oral splint therapy and pharmacotherapy. TMD will be assessed using the DC/TMD Axis I protocol. Evaluations will be performed at baseline, after the intervention period, and at 3- and 6-month follow-ups. All treatment protocols will last eight weeks. The primary outcome is pain intensity, assessed by the Numeric Rating Scale. Secondary outcomes include pain interference in daily life, jaw functional limitation, oral behaviors, anxiety, depression, and somatization (DC/TMD Axis II instruments). Sleep quality will be evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and salivary cortisol levels will serve as an exploratory physiological biomarker associated with stress response.
Data collection and analysis are ongoing; results will determine comparative treatment efficacy across all groups.
This is the first clinical trial to compare individualized acupuncture based on TCM with a standardized acupuncture protocol derived from Western diagnosis in the management of painful TMD. The findings are expected to contribute to evidence-based clinical practice and improve therapeutic decision-making for this complex condition.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture combined with traditional Chinese medicine therapy improves non-alcoholic steatohepatitis by regulating the TLR4/NF-κB and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways.
papers.authors: Mi L, Chen J, Li J, Gao F, Wang L, Dong Q et al.
papers.abstract: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), an advanced stage of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), is characterized by hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress, yet effective pharmacological therapies remain limited. The present study investigated the therapeutic effects and potential underlying mechanisms of electroacupuncture (EA) combined with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction in a high-fat diet-induced rat model of NASH. Rats were treated with EA, TCM decoction, or their combination, and liver pathology, biochemical parameters, transcriptomic profiles, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and related signaling pathways were comprehensively evaluated. Combined EA and TCM treatment markedly reduced liver weight and liver index, alleviated hepatic steatosis and histopathological injury, improved liver function by decreasing serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels, and ameliorated lipid and glucose metabolism disorders. Transcriptome sequencing identified 351 differentially expressed genes, with enrichment analyses indicating that inflammatory and oxidative stress-related pathways were potentially associated with the interventional effect. Molecular results showed that the combined treatment significantly suppressed the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway, resulting in decreased the expression of inflammatory mediators, and simultaneously activated the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway to enhance cellular antioxidant defense. In addition, HSD11B1 expression was markedly downregulated, suggesting its potential involvement in mediating the interplay between lipid metabolism and inflammatory responses during disease progression. Overall, in this high-fat diet-induced rat NASH model, EA combined with TCM decoction ameliorates NASH-related pathological alterations by regulating the TLR4/NF-κB and Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathways, improving hepatic pathology, restoring metabolic homeostasis, suppressing inflammation, and attenuating oxidative stress damage. This combined intervention regimen provides preclinical evidence for future studies on NASH therapy.

papers.title: [Development of an optimal acupuncture-moxibustion treatment protocol for perimenopausal insomnia].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Tian L, Wang Z, Chen Q, Li J, Yang X, Han J
papers.abstract:
To systematically evaluate various acupuncture-moxibustion treatment regimens for perimenopausal insomnia using network meta-analysis combined with multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) approach, and to identify interventions with optimal overall efficacy across multiple dimensions, so as to provide a scientific basis for clinical decision-making.
Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on acupuncture-moxibustion treatment for perimenopausal insomnia published from database inception to September 27, 2025 were systematically searched in the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Chinese Journal Service Platform (VIP), Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform, China Biology Medicine Database (SinoMed), PubMed, EMbase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. Network meta-analysis was performed using R software (version 4.4.3), and surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) value was calculated. A multidimensional evaluation system was established using the total effective rate, Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI) score, and modified Kupperman menopausal index (KMI) score as efficacy indexes, and treatment frequency as the cost index. The entropy weight method was applied to determine index weight, and the weighted normalized decision matrix was analyzed using technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) and multi-criteria optimization and compromise solution (Vlsekriterijumska Optimizacija I Kompromisno Resenje, VIKOR), two methods of MCDM, to comprehensively rank different acupuncture-moxibustion related interventions.
A total of 32 RCTs were finally eligible, involving 19 acupuncture-moxibustion related protocols and 3 control measures. Network meta-analysis showed: for the total effective rate, the cumulative ranking curve was high for depression-relieving acupuncture therapy combined with western medication (SUCRA = 0.76), mind-regulating acupuncture therapy combined with Chinese herbal medication (SUCRA=0.75), and acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle (SUCRA=0.75); for improvement in PSQI scores, cumulative ranking curve was high for abdominal acupuncture combined with Chinese herbal medication (SUCRA=0.93), depression-relieving acupuncture therapy combined with western medication (SUCRA=0.93), and acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle (SUCRA= 0.84); and for improvement in modified KMI scores, it was high for warm needling (SUCRA=0.95), time-based acupoint selection acupuncture (SUCRA=0.79), and scalp acupuncture (SUCRA=0.76). MCDM analysis on treatment frequency demonstrated that acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle ranked first in both TOPSIS and VIKOR methods, with relative closeness of 0.780 8 and Q value of 0, respectively.
Acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle demonstrates the advantages in both efficacy and cost, showing superior comprehensive performance among various acupuncture-moxibustion related interventions for perimenopausal insomnia, and it may serve as a clinically recommended option.

papers.title: [Compilation of extraordinary points based on 1963 edition of Illustrated Handbook of Extraordinary Points in Acupuncture and Moxibustion].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xu R, Zhuang R, Wu J, Li B
papers.abstract: This paper systematically investigates the compilation of the 1963 edition of Illustrated Handbook of Extraordinary Points in Acupuncture and Moxibustion through literature traceability and textual comparison study. This book has made significant contributions to the collection of literature on extraordinary points and content verification. However, some literature citations exhibited issues such as failing to trace the original sources, copying error on main indications of treatment, or bibliographic information misrepresentation; and there was a certain disconnect between the extensive compilation of literature and its subsequent processing. Hence, the paper explores how the compilation experience of Illustrated Handbook of Extraordinary Points in Acupuncture and Moxibustion can provide insights for contemporary research on the systematization of extraordinary points, and suggests enhancing the rigor and transparency of literature traceability and effectively utilizing digital tools to support research.

papers.title: [Return to a people-centered, individualized acupuncture diagnosis and treatment system].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Yu C, Niu Q, Liang S, Zhang L, Sun Y
papers.abstract: This article presents a review and commentary on technical generalization commonly existing in contemporary clinical acupuncture-moxibustion practice. The study highlights that clinical malpractice, "treating superficial or minor ailments using robust needle techniques (large needle)", not only leads to serious adverse outcomes including tissue damage and excessive depletion of qi and blood, but also deviates from the essential theories of TCM, which emphasizes the harmonization of yin and yang, and a patient-centered approach. By analyzing the current lack of the theory of "nine ancient needles", "each needle performs its specific function" in modern clinical practice, this study explores the underlying causes of this phenomenon from multiple dimensions including economic benefits, educational system, and research orientation; and proposes a solution for establishing an individualized treatment framework across three dimensions: reform in clinical practice, reconstruction of the teaching framework, and innovation in research standards. This paper emphasizes that only by returning to the classical concept of acupuncture and moxibustion, "comprehensive integrated treatment" and establishing a diagnostic and therapeutic evaluation system tailored to the characteristics of acupuncture and moxibustion, can the discipline of acupuncture and moxibustion achieve sustainable development and provide higher-quality healthcare services for human health.

papers.title: [Examination of folk acupuncture-moxibustion practice in the Song Dynasty based on Jiu Ai Tu].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang L
papers.abstract: As the earliest extant pictorial artwork depicting acupuncture-moxibustion-related medical customs, Jiu Ai Tu (Illustrations of Moxibustion and Acupuncture) provides invaluable visual historical materials for the study of the folk healthcare ecosystem during the Song Dynasty. From the perspective of medical iconography, the paper introduces a systematic interpretation of the physician-patient relationship, perceptions of disease, and therapeutic techniques of acupuncture and moxibustion depicted in this painting. By examining the identities of practitioners of traditional Chinese medicine, patient conditions, and various therapeutic approaches, including direct moxibustion with multiple cones, acupuncture for pus drainage, and external application of medicated plasters, this study reveals the interactive relationship between folk acupuncture practice during the Song Dynasty and the records preserved in medical texts. Furthermore, from a social historical standpoint, it explores the medical ecosystem of physician-patient relationship in the folk, the divergent fates of acupuncture-moxibustion therapies across different social strata, and the influence of the public dissemination of medical knowledge during the Song Dynasty, thereby providing a perspective from social history of knowledge for understanding the diverse dimensions of the medical society during the Song Dynasty.

papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Lian Y
papers.abstract: Although the theory of guimen thirteen needles is widely disseminated, its diverse origins and complex development have led to numerous opinions and interpretations. This article reviews the controversies regarding this theory across different historical periods and medical schools, and critically examines the views proposed by Bian Que, Ge Hong, Zhang Zhenren before the Tang Dynasty, as well as those put forward by Sun Zhenren and Xu Qiufu after the Tang Dynasty, so as to clarify the academic context and historical background of the theory of guimen thirteen needles, thereby refining the research on the origins of various interpretations of it. Furthermore, it is necessary to note the key cultural contexts associated and preserved in folk traditions regarding the various interpretations of the theory of guimen thirteen needles.

summary.results: 귀문 십삼침 이론은 시대별·학파별로 다양한 기원설과 해석이 전개되었으며, 민간 전승의 문화적 맥락도 함께 고려할 필요가 있음이 제시되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 논문은 귀문 십삼침의 임상효과를 검증하기보다 이론의 역사적 배경을 정리한 문헌이므로, 실제 침구 적용에는 별도의 근거 검토가 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 구체적 임상 데이터나 효과 비교 없이 역사적 해석을 중심으로 논의한 문헌이라는 점이 한계다.

papers.title: [Wentong Kangyan theory: interpretation and construction of theoretical model of moxibustion effect based on chronic vascular inflammation].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xu Q, Zhang T, Song X, Wang H, Hu X, Gao S et al.
papers.abstract: The paper addresses the explanatory predicament regarding the lack of logical coherence between the theory of moxibustion for warming and unblocking blood vessels and the pathology of chronic vascular inflammation, a theoretical model of Wentong Kangyan (warming and unblocking blood vessels for anti-inflammation) was constructed by systematically integrating biological evidence. This model elucidates the effect of moxibustion as a sequential biological process. Using surface thermal stimulation as a physical activation signal (promoting blood circulation by warming action of moxibustion), moxibustion activates the neuro-immune-vascular network to achieve systemic inflammatory homeostatic remodeling (anti-inflammation by warming and unblocking action) and specifically mediates improvement in vascular endothelial function (unblocking blood vessel and promoting blood circulation). This structured pathway, "body surface activation- systemic regulation-targeting effect", not only provides a logically consistent interpretation of classical theory based on modern science, but also demonstrates the construction pathway for transforming traditional acupuncture-moxibustion wisdom into verifiable theoretical model, representing a conscious practice to advance acupuncture-moxibustion research from empirical description towards theoretical formalization.

summary.question: 뜸의 온경통맥·항염 효과를 만성 혈관염증과 어떻게 논리적으로 연결할 수 있는지 검토한 연구이다.
summary.methods: 생물학적 근거를 체계적으로 통합하여 뜸 효과를 표면 열자극-신경면역혈관 네트워크-혈관 기능 개선의 순차적 과정으로 설명하는 이론모델을 구축한 이론 연구이다.
summary.results: 뜸은 표면 열자극으로 시작해 전신 염증 항상성 재조정과 혈관 내피기능 개선으로 이어지는 ‘체표 활성화-전신 조절-표적 효과’ 경로로 해석되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 전통적 뜸 이론을 현대 생물학과 연결해 설명하려는 시도로, 임상 해석의 틀을 제공하지만 직접적 치료효과를 입증한 근거로 보기는 어렵다.
summary.limitations: 생물학적 근거를 바탕으로 한 이론모델 구축 연구이므로 실제 환자에서의 임상적 유효성은 검증되지 않았다.

papers.title: [Approach of the "three-adjustment" acupuncture and moxibustion to autonomic nervous system dysfunction based on the "regulating brain-mind, regulating heart-mind, and regulating spleen- stomach"].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Shen T, Xiao Z, Li Y, Yu X, Wang Z
papers.abstract: Autonomic nervous system dysfunction (ANSD) primarily manifests as symptoms such as insomnia, tinnitus, palpitations, chest tightness, and dyspepsia. Acupuncture and moxibustion exert the effects of unblocking meridians and harmonizing yin and yang, and hold unique advantages and clinical value in treatment of ANSD. Based on its common clinical manifestations and TCM theory regarding zangfu organs, it is viewed that the core pathogenesis of ANSD is characterized by "impairment of brain-mind in coordination, heart-mind disturbance, and dysfunction of spleen and stomach". Based on this, "three-adjustment" acupuncture and moxibustion, "regulating brain-mind, regulating heart-mind, and regulating spleen-stomach", is proposed as the general therapeutic principle for "mind adjustment", taking both form and mind into consideration and treating both root and branch. Clinically, Baihui (GV20) and Fengchi (GB20) are used to regulate the brain-mind; Neiguan (PC6) and Shenmen (HT7) are used to regulate the heart-mind; Zusanli (ST36) and Shangjuxu (ST37) are to regulate the spleen and stomach. Mind is primarily regulated prior to the body, and deqi and gentle stimulation are required specifically. Modern studies suggest that the three groups of core acupoints are involved in the regulation of autonomic nervous function through central nervous system, cardiac autonomic nervous system, and vagus nerve, providing a solid foundation of modern research for the clinical application of "three-adjustment" method of acupuncture and moxibustion. Such therapy adopts an integrated approach to "brain-heart-spleen-stomach" system, centers at "mind adjustment", and offers a novel perspective for treatment of ANSD with acupuncture and moxibustion.

summary.methods: 자율신경계 기능장애의 임상 증상과 중의학 장부 이론, 그리고 현대 연구를 바탕으로 침구 치료 원칙과 핵심 혈위를 제안한 서술적 임상 논문이다.
summary.results: 삼조절 침구는 뇌-심장-비위 축을 통합적으로 조절하여 자율신경 기능을 개선할 가능성이 있으며, 관련 핵심 혈위의 현대적 기전 근거가 제시되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 자율신경계 기능장애에서 침구의 임상 적용은 뇌-심장-비위의 통합 조절이라는 관점에서 이해할 수 있으나, 실제 효과는 추가 임상 근거로 확인이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 실제 비교시험이나 정량적 임상 결과가 제시되지 않은 이론·고찰 중심의 논문이다.

papers.title: [ZHUANG Lixing's clinical experience for sudden hearing loss with the "regulating the spirit and restoring the pivot" acupuncture method].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Han M, Liao K, Zhan J, Zeng Y, Zhuang L
papers.abstract: This article summarizes Professor ZHUANG Lixing 's clinical experience for sudden hearing loss with the "regulating the spirit and restoring the pivot" acupuncture method. Professor ZHUANG considers that the disease is mostly caused by emotional disturbance and dysfunction of the Shaoyang pivot, and advocates early acupuncture and moxibustion intervention. The pathogenesis of "closure of the orifices and concealment of the spirit as the manifestation, and impaired pivot mechanism as the root" should be closely followed, and the therapeutic principle of "regulating the spirit as the priority and restoring the pivot as the key" should be applied. In clinical practice, acupoints on the governor vessel, such as Shenting (GV24) and Yintang (GV24+), are selected to regulate the spirit, while acupoints on the Shaoyang meridians, such as Tinghui (GB2) and Yifeng (TE17), are selected to restore the pivot, supplemented by flexible selection of additional acupoints according to the presenting pattern. Together, these methods open the orifices and relieve obstruction, unblock the ear, and restore hearing.

papers.title: [YANG Jun's clinical experience in treating rotational spasmodic torticollis through differentiation on pathogenesis, sinews/fascia of meridians and muscles].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zhang J, Xiao H, Zhang Q, Cui J, Huang Z, Zhang L et al.
papers.abstract: The paper introduces Professor YANG Jun 's clinical experience in diagnosis and treatment of rotational spasmodic torticollis with acupuncture and moxibustion. Professor YANG believes that this disorder is rooted in yang deficiency, manifesting clinically as disturbances caused by internal and external wind pathogens. The crucial factor lies on the impaired distribution of the governor vessel, and the location of disorder is on sinews/fascia of meridians. Under the general principle of "yang deficiency with wind agitation", it is essential to precisely differentiate three syndromes/patterns, including cold-dampness obstructing the collaterals, yin deficiency stirring up wind, and phlegm-stasis obstructing the collaterals. The treatment approach focuses on regulating yang and unblocking the governor vessel, as well as relaxing tendons and relieving spasms; and it emphasizes a layered therapeutic strategy based on three distinct levels, i.e., identifying the underlying pathogenic mechanism, assessing the affected sinews/fascia of meridians, and determining the targeted muscle groups. Differentiating pathogenesis is to distinguish the deficiency of root causes from the excess of clinical symptoms, differentiating sinews/fascia of meridians is to determine the location of illness, and differentiating muscles serves to identify the affected muscle groups. In treatment, the local acupoints are selected precisely and combined with the distal ones based on meridian distribution, the appropriate acupoints are used in accordance with the specific syndromes/patterns, the acupoints of the governor vessel are especially combined with scalp acupuncture. In operation, transverse needling, point-toward-point needling, surrounding needling and bone-targeting needle techniques are employed. All the aforementioned provide the references for clinical diagnosis and treatment of rotational spasmodic torticollis.

papers.title: [WANG Jihong's experience in treatment of thyroid nodules with Tongyuan acupuncture therapy and "five acupoints from tianyou"].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Huang S, Li Z, Huang Z, Li H, Wang J, Hou J
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Professor WANG Jihong's clinical experience in treatment of thyroid nodules with Tongyuan acupuncture therapy and "five acupoints from tianyou". Based on the theoretical framework of "mind/spirit, qi, the origin and body", as well as the holistic idea of TCM such as "nourishing mind/spirit" and "guiding qi ", thyroid nodules are treated in stages. In the early stage, the acupoints for unblocking the governor vessel and nourishing mind/spirit are selected, including Baihui (GV20), Yintang (CV24+), Dazhui (GV14), and Zhiyang (GV9). In the later stage, the acupoints for guiding qi back to the origin are selected, such as Guanyuan (CV4), Qihai (CV6), Danzhong (CV17), and Tianshu (ST25). Throughout the entire course of treatment, Renying (ST9) and Futu (LI18), two of the key points from "five acupoints from tianyou" documented in the Huangdi Neijing (Yellow Emperor 's Inner Classic) are incorporated to regulate qi movement and resolve tangible pathogenic accumulations in the neck region. This distinctive therapeutic approach embodies the principles of "addressing both symptoms and root cause simultaneously" and "mutual regulation of body and qi " in treatment. It not only alleviates the symptoms of thyroid nodules but also restores the dynamic equilibrium of "mind/spirit, qi, the origin and body", so as to reduce local lesion size, and the risk of malignant transformation, thereby obtaining the specific therapeutic effect of TCM, "prevention before disease onset, and prevention of progression after onset".
